main_body: Flat ground patch of beige and pink brick-style paving with grey mortar gaps, plus a few blue-grey rectangles and dark strips with grey/white blocks along the top-right and left edges
top_band: none. This is a flat terrain paving pattern with no standing volume, so there is no top band above a front face
evidence: The candidate is a terrain tile set (ground paving), not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-and-front construction does not apply. No isometric side faces, no elevation of a body, and no slab with a missing front. The dark strips and grey blocks at the top-right and left are tile-edge fragments, not a standing volume.

style.evidence: The brick ramps have about 4 steps: light beige, a pinkish mid, a dark grey mortar and a few blue-grey patches. The grass and cobble references have about 5-6 steps with per-stone shading and grain. Many brick faces are flat fills of one beige, for example the 5x5+ blocks around rows 12-15 and 28-31. The mortar and gaps are neutral dark grey, which reads as a uniform outline rather than a tinted dark material tone. The pattern repeats mechanically with little per-brick highlight or speckle. The blue-grey rectangles and the dark strips with white/grey blocks look like stray artifacts rather than coherent materials. Tiles carry only about 3-5 colours each, well below the reference's roughly 10 per tile.
